summary: Pier light at the lake entrance to the Sturgeon Bay Ship Canal, Door County, Wisconsin: lit 1882, tower rebuilt 1903, automated 1972, sold at a federal auction in 2014.

lens.where: original optic; fifth-order lens from 1900 (LighthouseFriends); current optic 300 mm (Archive)

structures.type: cylindrical tower on square fog-signal house

access.note: Archive: not open to the public. LighthouseFriends: pier open, dwelling and tower closed. Route runs through the Coast Guard station.

visit.note: Tower closed to visitors (LighthouseFriends). Do not climb.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard (aid to navigation, per 2014 FOX 11 report); LighthouseFriends' visitor note says privately owned; ownership after the 2014 auction not confirmed by sources read

events.note: First tower, wooden frame, built October and November 1881 (LighthouseFriends).
Lit 15 May 1882 with a sixth-order Fresnel lens (LighthouseFriends).
Steam whistle on the pier shoreward of the light.
Piers under fog signal No. 1 (10 March) and No. 2 (23 March) caught fire.
Fifth-order Fresnel replaced the original sixth-order lens (LighthouseFriends).
Combined light and fog signal tower on the pier end; tested early September 1903.
Electrified; fog signal changed to an air diaphone; radiobeacon added (LighthouseFriends).
Coast Guard declared the light excess; offered at no cost to eligible federal, state and local agencies and nonprofit groups; no qualified steward found.
Online federal auction; high bid $48,500 by Gordon Krist of Paris, Kentucky; closing not complete in early October 2014 (FOX 11). LighthouseFriends gives the auction close as 12 September 2014.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1882 is the first light (LighthouseFriends: lit 15 May 1882; Archive: original lens 1882). 1903 is the current combined light and fog-signal tower (Archive, FOX 11, LighthouseFriends). Both dates are used in the story.
Archive roster: principal keeper 1886 to 1899. LighthouseFriends: 1886 to 1910, died at the station in spring 1910. Both are recorded in the roster lines.

Two Board fog-signal rows for Sturgeon Bay Canal differ because they cover different years: 355 hours for the year ended 30 June 1891 (scan 176) and about 381 hours for the year ended 30 June 1892 (scan 510). LighthouseFriends' about 540 hours a year is undated and not reconciled with either.

notes_for_editor: Story: us-wi-sturgeon-bay-canal-north-pierhead.md. Length: moderate-to-rich (about 1,000 words, 4 chapters plus Today). Open disagreements, left open in the story: (a) tower material, cast iron (Archive, FOX 11) vs quarter-inch steel plate (LighthouseFriends); (b) fog-whistle running time: the Board's 1892 table (scan 510) gives about 381 hours for the year ended 30 June 1892 and its 1891 table (scan 176) gives 355 hours for the year ended 30 June 1891; LighthouseFriends gives about 540 hours a year (undated); (c) Chapman's end date, 1899 (Archive) vs 1910 (LighthouseFriends); (d) pier access, open (LighthouseFriends) vs not open to the public (Archive); (e) 2014 sale: FOX 11 says closing had not occurred in early October 2014; LighthouseFriends says the auction closed 12 September 2014 with Krist as winner. Ownership now is unknown. Name variant: LighthouseFriends prints the first keeper as Rufus M. Wright; the Archive says Rufus J. Wright. The story uses the Archive form. Record fixes to check: structure year and height (see corrections); the record's 'horn' fog signal conflicts with the air diaphone of 1930 (LighthouseFriends). Page checks: printed page numbers for Board scan pages 501 and 510 are OCR guesses ('?' in the corpus); look at the page images before publishing. The Board's 1891-92 OCR text on scan 501 is garbled in places ('powtf', 'nortii'); quotes copy the OCR as printed. Not used: the Coast Guard Historian's page for the light (archived copies returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text); Wikipedia (lead only). Chronicling America searches for the light in Wisconsin papers, 1880-1915, gave no usable station page. Life-Saving Service station 'Sturgeon Bay Canal' is a separate station from the light; only the 1888 Dreadnaught entry is tied to the north pier. Roster: USLHS lines (cite 4, with person slugs) plus LighthouseFriends stints from 1899 on (cite 5, no slugs), from its keeper list; LighthouseFriends' open-ended entries (Klaus L. Andersen, Robert Sterritt) are omitted. Photos: none new. Access and safety: the approach crosses Coast Guard property; the story says so.
